title: Retrofit CAM_ISSUE_RESULT machine line onto cam issue --file-local and list (deterministic-CLI handback consistency)
description: Follow-up surfaced during the CAM-210 grill (2026-07-07). CAM-210 adds a machine-parseable CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>/=ERROR line to the new `cam issue close`/`abandon` subcommands (the CAM-197 structured-handback thesis). The sibling deterministic paths `cam issue --file-local` (index.ts:1372-1414) and `cam issue list` predate that thesis and emit only a human printHint + exit code, no CAM_ISSUE_* line. This leaves the deterministic `cam issue` surface inconsistent: some subcommands hand back a parseable line, some don't. Retrofit the machine line onto --file-local (CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id> on result.ok, CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR on failure, alongside the existing `filed <id> on main (<sha>)` hint) and decide/apply the appropriate handback for `list`. Keep printHint for humans. Origin: operator-approved during CAM-210 spec; concrete Layer-1 instance of the CAM-197 epic.

spec.scope: Retrofit the CAM_ISSUE_RESULT machine handback line onto `cam issue --file-local` inside dispatchIssue (index.ts), mirroring the close/abandon convention from CAM-210. Success emits `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>` on stdout right after the existing `filed <id> on main (<sha>)` printHint; the three failure sites each emit `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=<token>`. The reason token comes from the createLocalIssueOnMain discriminated union for the create-failure case, plus `invalid-json` for the stdin JSON.parse failure (emitted before the create runs) and `exception` for the catch block. `cam issue list` is deliberately left WITHOUT a CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line: its handback stays the rendered table + exit code, because CAM_ISSUE_RESULT is a mutation-outcome contract (the id of the single acted-on issue, or ERROR) and list is a read over many issues with no id. Out of scope: close/abandon (already done in CAM-210), createLocalIssueOnMain and runIssueList internals, any new flags, and any speculative machine token for list.
acceptanceCriteria: `cam issue --file-local` on success writes BOTH the existing `filed <id> on main (<sha>)` printHint AND a `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=<id>` line to stdout, exit 0.

`cam issue --file-local` when createLocalIssueOnMain returns { ok:false, reason } writes `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=<reason>` to stdout with reason one of diverged|detached-head|missing-main|guardrail-failed, exit 1.
`cam issue --file-local` with unparseable JSON on stdin writes `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=invalid-json` to stdout, exit 1.
`cam issue --file-local` when the create path throws (catch block) writes `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT=ERROR reason=exception` to stdout, exit 1.
`cam issue list` emits NO `CAM_ISSUE_RESULT` line on any code path; its output remains the rendered table and the process exit code is the sole machine signal.

The machine line is written via process.stdout.write (not printHint/printError), and the pre-existing printHint on success plus any pre-existing printError on failure are preserved (human hint and machine line coexist, exactly like close/abandon at index.ts:1489/1493/1502/1506).

Unit tests assert the exact CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line for each --file-local outcome (success id line; each of the four error reason tokens) via injected fakes, and a test asserts `cam issue list` produces no CAM_ISSUE_RESULT line.
Quality gates green: `bun run typecheck` zero errors, `bun test` all pass, `bun run check:all` (biome lint --error-on-warnings included) passes.
gotchas: The current --file-local result.ok===false path does NOT read result.reason (comment: 'printError already fired inside createLocalIssueOnMain'); the retrofit must now read result.reason for the machine line while leaving that pre-existing printError intact. The machine line is additive, not a replacement of the human error output.

`invalid-json` is a persist-specific reason token emitted BEFORE createLocalIssueOnMain runs (the stdin JSON.parse fails first), mirroring CAM-213's spec-persist convention. It is NOT a member of the createLocalIssueOnMain reason union.
The machine line must go to stdout via process.stdout.write, the same channel close/abandon use, never printHint/printError (those are human channels and biome/tests key on the exact machine string).
The `list` no-line outcome is a deliberate design decision, not a forgotten path: encode it in an explicit AC and a regression test so a future reviewer does not flag list as an omission.
noUncheckedIndexedAccess is on repo-wide; guard any array/regex-group access touched by the change.
